title: Getting started
description: From signing up to publishing your first chart: follow this guide to find out how to use Graph Italia.

account.title: Sign up and log in
items: In the top right corner, click Log in and create your account with your email address: you will receive a verification code to activate it.
Every account already has a personal project; you can create more and share them with other people through the Organizations feature.

create.title: Create a new item
items: In your private area click Create new and choose the kind of item you want to create: a chart, a KPI group, a map, a dashboard or a data source.
Give your item a title and, if needed, add a description to make it easier to identify. Both can be changed from the editor.

data.title: Import your data
items: In Load your data you can import your data from a CSV or JSON file, or link the information from an external URL.

After loading, review the table structure and adjust it if needed. You can filter and reorder columns, rename headers, transpose rows and columns. Please note: if the data has repeated rows, the editor suggests an aggregation of the data (count, sum or mean).

configure.title: Configure the chart
items: Choose the kind of chart you want to create among bars, lines, pie or map, and watch the preview build up as you go.
You can configure and customize your chart with the available settings. In Advanced settings you can create and set up tooltip, grid and axes.
In the Info section you define the chart visibility: if public it can be seen by anyone with the direct link and embedded in other websites, if private it stays visible to you only.

publish.title: Save, publish and share
items: Once your changes are done click Save: your chart will appear in the list of your personal projects in the private area.
If you created a chart with public visibility, in the Share column you can copy the public link and the embed code (iframe) to integrate in your website.

dashboard.title: Compose a dashboard
items: A dashboard collects several charts and text blocks in a single page: you can drag the items into the grid slots, adjust heights and widths and write the texts.
A dashboard can be shared with a public link.

api.title: Information for developers
items: From the menu you can generate an API key (read-only or read/write) to use the project's REST APIs.
Data sources are datasets that can be reused and updated via API too: they are useful to feed data from a script or an external system.

footer.text: That is all you need to get started: for everything else, each section has contextual help texts.
